newsitem.title: USA: Multiple crash on foggy Florida bridge kills one.
newsitem.headline: Multiple crash on foggy Florida bridge kills one.

text.p: One person was killed and 26 people were injured when dozens of cars crashed on a fog-bound bridge over Tampa Bay Friday, the Florida Highway Patrol said.

The multiple collisions occured on both the north and southbound lanes of the Skyway bridge and causeway, which runs for about 16 miles (26 km) across the mouth of the bay to link St. Petersburg and Sarasota.
Wrecked vehicles were spread out in clusters over about 1.5 miles (2.5 km), Chuck Kearns, spokesman for Sunstar Emergency Medical Services, told Reuters.

Highway Patrol spokesman Lt. Harry Mofield said a 69-year-old woman had died and Kearns said 26 other people were taken to hospitals, five or six of them in critical condition. Among them was an 11-month-old girl said to be in serious condition.

The accident occured just before 11:30 a.m. as busy traffic was struggling through zero-visibility fog rolling in from the Gulf of Mexico. "The accident was first called in for 15 vehicles but it wound up a lot more," Kearns said. "It was on both the northbound and southbound."
The Highway Patrol said 38 cars and 16 trucks or vans were involved. One truck was a car-carrier that spilled its load.

The fog prevented rescue helicopters from taking off for a time but eventually they evacuated four injured people. Firefighters laid ladders across the 50-foot gap between the causeways to reach some victims because the road was blocked.
"It looked like a parking lot," one witness said.
Both spans of the bridge, which reaches heights of up to 180 feet to allow ships to pass through, were closed.
